capabilities.architectureNotes: Foundation of IaaS. All three providers offer comparable general-purpose and memory-optimized shapes. Hybrid extension (Outposts, Arc, Distributed Cloud) differentiates at enterprise scale.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: Patching overhead scales with fleet size. Reserved/committed pricing requires capacity planning discipline. Sole-tenant/dedicated options incur premium.

capabilities.architectureNotes: Event-driven compute abstraction. AWS Lambda has the largest ecosystem and most mature tooling. Azure Durable Functions provides strong stateful workflow support. GCP Cloud Run offers container-native serverless with stronger portability.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: Cold start latency matters for latency-sensitive workloads. Debugging distributed serverless functions requires mature observability strategy. Cost can surprise at high invocation volume without concurrency controls.

tierNotes.Enterprise: VPC, SnapStart, arm64; Provisioned Concurrency; EventBridge Pipes

tierNotes.Government: Azure Government; FedRAMP High; DISA IL2/IL4

capabilities.architectureNotes: IAM is the architectural foundation everything else depends on. Azure's Entra ID is tightly coupled to the Microsoft ecosystem and assumed by most Azure services. AWS IAM offers the most granular policy model. GCP's IAM integrates with Google Workspace identity. All three support workforce federation and PIV/CAC for government.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: Misconfigured IAM is the most common enterprise cloud security failure mode. Permission boundaries, SCPs, and resource control policies are essential at scale. PIV/CAC integration requires specific configuration in all three providers.

tierNotes.Personal / Free: IAM (free); IAM Identity Center (free)
tierNotes.Commercial / SMB: IAM + Identity Center + Cognito; SCP via Organizations
tierNotes.Enterprise: Permission Boundaries + SCPs + Resource Control Policies; Verified Access (ZTNA)
tierNotes.Government: GovCloud; PIV/CAC via Identity Center; FedRAMP High; CJIS

tierNotes.Enterprise: Entra ID P2 (PIM, Identity Protection, Entitlement Mgmt); External ID for B2B
tierNotes.Government: Entra ID Government; PIV/CAC; HSPD-12; EO 14028 MFA; FedRAMP High; DISA

tierNotes.Personal / Free: Cloud IAM (free); Google Workspace Identity free tier
tierNotes.Commercial / SMB: Cloud IAM + Cloud Identity + BeyondCorp (Context-Aware Access)
tierNotes.Enterprise: Cloud IAM + VPC-SC + Access Context Manager; Workforce Identity Federation
tierNotes.Government: Assured Workloads; PIV/CAC via Workforce Identity Federation

capabilities.architectureNotes: Foundational storage for data lakes, backup, static assets, and archival. AWS S3 is the de facto standard with the widest ecosystem integration. Azure Blob has strong Microsoft data platform integration. GCS excels with BigQuery native integration. Egress costs are a significant architectural consideration at scale.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: Egress costs can become substantial at scale. Lifecycle policies are essential for cost control. Object Lock / WORM is important for compliance. Bucket-level public access should be denied by default in enterprise.

tierNotes.Commercial / SMB: Standard/IA/Glacier/Deep Archive; Intelligent-Tiering auto-moves
tierNotes.Enterprise: S3 + Replication + Object Lock; Access Points; Macie for PII; S3 Inventory
tierNotes.Government: S3 GovCloud + Object Lock; FedRAMP High; ITAR; CJIS

tierNotes.Personal / Free: 5 GB LRS free (12 months)

tierNotes.Enterprise: Blob + Immutable Storage + Lifecycle Mgmt; Blob index tags; Azure Defender
tierNotes.Government: Azure Blob Government; FedRAMP High; Sovereign regions

capabilities.architectureNotes: GKE is widely considered the most mature managed Kubernetes offering given Google's authorship of Kubernetes. AKS has strong Azure ecosystem integration and free control plane. EKS has the broadest enterprise adoption in AWS shops. All support hybrid extension (Anthos, Arc, Outposts/EKS Anywhere).
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: Kubernetes carries significant operational burden even in managed form. Dedicated platform engineering capability is recommended at enterprise scale. Networking complexity (CNI, service mesh, ingress) is a common friction point. Control plane costs vary significantly.

tierNotes.Personal / Free: No free tier; ECS control plane free
tierNotes.Commercial / SMB: EKS / ECS / App Runner; $0.10/hr cluster fee; Fargate or EC2 nodes
tierNotes.Enterprise: EKS Anywhere + EKS Distro; Hybrid; BottleRocket OS; Karpenter autoscaling
tierNotes.Government: EKS GovCloud; FedRAMP High; DoD IL2/IL4/IL5

capabilities.architectureNotes: Aurora (AWS) leads on performance/cost for MySQL/PostgreSQL workloads. Azure SQL has the strongest SQL Server compatibility and enterprise licensing path (Hybrid Benefit). Spanner (GCP) is unique for globally consistent ACID at scale but with significant lock-in.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: Multi-region HA adds cost and complexity. Read replicas don't provide write HA. RDS Custom (AWS) and Managed Instance (Azure) support lift-and-shift for Oracle/SQL Server with less re-architecture. Cloud Spanner has unique pricing model that requires capacity planning.

tierNotes.Commercial / SMB: RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB, ElastiCache; Aurora Serverless v2
tierNotes.Enterprise: Aurora Global DB; DynamoDB Global Tables; RDS Custom for Oracle/SQL Server

capabilities.architectureNotes: Azure OpenAI has the strongest enterprise/gov deployment story for GPT models. AWS Bedrock provides the widest multi-model choice (Claude, Llama, Mistral, Titan, Nova) without model lock-in. GCP Vertex AI GenAI is tightly integrated with Google data/analytics stack. Government availability is the most active area of parity lag across all three providers.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: Token costs scale rapidly with usage volume. Prompt engineering and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) are operationally non-trivial. Data residency and model data retention policies differ significantly and require legal review for regulated workloads. Content filtering and guardrails are essential before enterprise deployment.

tierNotes.Personal / Free: No free tier; pay per token; playground only
tierNotes.Commercial / SMB: Claude, Llama, Mistral, Titan, Nova; Agents; Knowledge Bases; Guardrails; Flows
tierNotes.Enterprise: Provisioned Throughput; Model Eval; Watermark; Custom Model Import; Model Distillation
tierNotes.Government: Bedrock GovCloud limited/expanding; FedRAMP Moderate baseline; IL coverage expanding

capabilities.architectureNotes: Microsoft Sentinel is the most mature cloud-native SIEM with the broadest connector ecosystem. Chronicle (GCP) is purpose-built for petabyte-scale log ingestion with Google threat intelligence. AWS Security Hub is an aggregator, not a full SIEM — third-party or OpenSearch-based solutions are common in AWS environments.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: SIEM implementation requires dedicated security operations expertise. Log ingestion costs are a significant operational consideration at scale. Integration with identity systems and incident response workflows is essential. Cloud-native SIEMs reduce infrastructure overhead but increase vendor dependency.

capabilities.architectureNotes: BigQuery (GCP) offers the best serverless analytics experience and tightest ML integration. Redshift (AWS) is deeply embedded in the AWS data ecosystem and has strong RA3 instance performance. Synapse and Microsoft Fabric (Azure) provide the best integration with Power BI, Office 365, and Microsoft enterprise data estates.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: Query costs in on-demand models can surprise without governance guardrails. Slot/reservation pricing requires capacity planning. Data egress for cross-cloud or on-prem data movement adds cost. Schema design for distributed analytics differs significantly from traditional RDBMS patterns.

tierNotes.Commercial / SMB: Redshift + EMR + Glue + Kinesis + QuickSight; Lake Formation governance
tierNotes.Enterprise: Redshift Serverless + RA3; Lake Formation; Clean Rooms
tierNotes.Government: Redshift GovCloud + Glue GovCloud; FedRAMP High

capabilities.architectureNotes: AWS Transfer Family is the only native cloud MFT service among the three. GCP and Azure lack native MFT equivalents — both rely on partner solutions (GoAnywhere, MuleSoft, Axway). For API management, Apigee (GCP) is the most full-featured. Azure APIM is deeply integrated with the Microsoft enterprise stack.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: MFT solutions often handle regulated data (CJIS, HIPAA, PII). AS2 for EDI, SFTP for legacy agency integrations, and HTTPS for modern APIs are common in government. Protocol support breadth and audit logging are critical differentiators for compliance. GoAnywhere and similar tools can bridge all three clouds.

tierNotes.Commercial / SMB: Transfer Family SFTP/FTPS/AS2; SQS/SNS/MQ/Step Functions/EventBridge
tierNotes.Enterprise: Transfer Family Enterprise; AppFlow; B2B Messaging (EDI); EventBridge Pipes
tierNotes.Government: Transfer Family GovCloud; SQS/SNS GovCloud; MuleSoft GovCloud on AWS

capabilities.architectureNotes: Azure DevOps + GitHub (both Microsoft) provide the most integrated enterprise CI/CD ecosystem. AWS CodePipeline is native to AWS but CodeCommit is no longer accepting new customers (July 2024). GCP Cloud Build is solid but less feature-rich than competing platforms — many GCP shops use GitHub Actions or GitLab CI.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: Supply chain security (SBOM, Binary Authorization, secret scanning) is increasingly a compliance requirement. STIG-hardened build environments are required for government IL2/IL4. DISA STIG-compliant pipeline patterns are available for all three providers. CodeCommit deprecation is a migration concern for existing AWS CI/CD investments.

tierNotes.Commercial / SMB: CodeBuild + CodeDeploy + CodePipeline + CodeArtifact + CodeGuru
tierNotes.Enterprise: CodeCatalyst; CodeGuru Security; Inspector SBOM export; Binary Authorization
tierNotes.Government: CodePipeline/CodeBuild/CodeDeploy GovCloud; FedRAMP High; DISA STIG build environments

capabilities.architectureNotes: Virtual networks provide private address spaces, routing, security boundaries, and private connectivity patterns. CDN and edge controls should be selected alongside the network design because internet egress, origin protection, and regulated routing requirements affect architecture.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: Track internet and cross-region egress costs, centralize network policy ownership, and validate edge or private-connectivity features in the target regulated environment before relying on them.

aws.sourceNotes: Amazon VPC is documented in AWS GovCloud (US); this row does not assert feature parity for the broader networking and edge design without a service-by-service review.

tierNotes.Personal / Free: Use a minimal VPC layout and review public-IP and egress charges before deployment.
tierNotes.Commercial / SMB: Add centralized routing, private endpoints, edge delivery, and web application controls as needed.
tierNotes.Enterprise: Evaluate shared network hubs, private connectivity, traffic inspection, and egress governance.
tierNotes.Government: Confirm each required network and edge component in AWS GovCloud documentation before design approval.

azure.sourceNotes: Azure Government publishes current product availability separately; verify every required networking and edge component for the selected government environment.

tierNotes.Personal / Free: Use a small virtual network design and inspect billable gateways or outbound traffic.
tierNotes.Commercial / SMB: Add private access, controlled ingress, and edge delivery based on application exposure.
tierNotes.Enterprise: Evaluate hub-and-spoke or virtual WAN patterns, ExpressRoute, security inspection, and policy controls.
tierNotes.Government: Use the Azure Government availability roadmap for the specific network services in scope.

gcp.sourceNotes: Assured Workloads support is control-package specific; verify VPC and any edge services against the selected package before regulated deployment.

tierNotes.Personal / Free: Use a small VPC design and review network service and outbound traffic pricing.
tierNotes.Commercial / SMB: Add managed load balancing, private access, and edge controls when public workloads require them.
tierNotes.Enterprise: Evaluate shared VPC, private connectivity, centralized security policy, and network cost controls.
tierNotes.Government: Confirm allowed network services in the applicable Assured Workloads control package.

capabilities.architectureNotes: Managed metrics, logging, tracing, alerting, and dashboards form the operational evidence layer for cloud workloads. A portable telemetry strategy can reduce migration friction while provider-native tools simplify service integration.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: Define log retention, sampling, alert ownership, and access controls early. Telemetry ingestion and retention can become material operating costs, especially when audit retention requirements apply.

aws.govVariant: Amazon CloudWatch Logs in AWS GovCloud (US)
aws.sourceNotes: AWS documents CloudWatch Logs in AWS GovCloud (US) with feature differences; validate the required CloudWatch features beyond logs for the target workload.

tierNotes.Personal / Free: Start with essential metrics, alarms, and limited log retention.
tierNotes.Commercial / SMB: Standardize dashboards, alert routing, audit logs, and application telemetry.
tierNotes.Enterprise: Establish central observability ownership, retention policy, access governance, and cost controls.
tierNotes.Government: Review AWS GovCloud feature differences and retention obligations before implementation.

azure.sourceNotes: Microsoft documents Azure Monitor usage in Azure Government and publishes availability by service; verify required Monitor components in the current government roadmap.

tierNotes.Personal / Free: Capture essential metrics and retain only necessary logs.
tierNotes.Commercial / SMB: Use common workspaces, alerts, application telemetry, and operational dashboards.
tierNotes.Enterprise: Govern retention, query access, export, and multicloud or hybrid telemetry patterns.
tierNotes.Government: Confirm each Azure Monitor component in the Azure Government availability roadmap.

gcp.govVariant: Cloud Monitoring under Assured Workloads control packages
gcp.sourceNotes: Google documents Cloud Monitoring support under Assured Workloads with limitations for some features; verify the selected control package and telemetry feature set.

tierNotes.Personal / Free: Capture essential metrics and logs with deliberate retention.
tierNotes.Commercial / SMB: Standardize log routing, alerts, service dashboards, and trace collection.
tierNotes.Enterprise: Govern sinks, retention, telemetry access, and cost controls across projects.
tierNotes.Government: Check Cloud Monitoring and Logging support for the selected Assured Workloads package.

capabilities.architectureNotes: Government and sovereign offerings use provider-specific tenancy, boundary, eligibility, and control models. A comparable workload design must start from the required control regime and supported service inventory rather than assume commercial-cloud equivalence.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: Confirm account eligibility, identity boundaries, region selection, authorized services, support access constraints, and procurement requirements before selecting a regulated cloud deployment model.

aws.sourceNotes: AWS GovCloud (US) is a documented offering; commercial-to-GovCloud parity must be evaluated service by service for a given architecture.

tierNotes.Personal / Free: Government environment eligibility and onboarding requirements apply.
tierNotes.Commercial / SMB: Use standard AWS regions unless a regulated workload requires GovCloud eligibility and controls.
tierNotes.Enterprise: Map required services, identities, integrations, and operational boundaries before migration.
tierNotes.Government: Use the GovCloud service documentation and compliance materials for the required control regime.

azure.sourceNotes: Azure Government is a documented physically isolated cloud; use Microsoft's current availability roadmap to establish feature support for each workload.

tierNotes.Personal / Free: Government environment eligibility and onboarding requirements apply.
tierNotes.Commercial / SMB: Use commercial Azure unless the workload requires Azure Government controls and eligibility.
tierNotes.Enterprise: Map dependencies to the current Azure Government availability roadmap before migration.
tierNotes.Government: Confirm services and impact-level requirements in Microsoft government documentation.

gcp.sourceNotes: Assured Workloads uses control packages with product-specific support; it is not represented here as a separate government cloud partition or universal parity claim.

tierNotes.Personal / Free: Regulated control packages require workload and eligibility review.
tierNotes.Commercial / SMB: Select control packages only where regulatory or sovereignty requirements warrant them.
tierNotes.Enterprise: Map each required service to the applicable Assured Workloads supported-product list.
tierNotes.Government: Validate control package, allowed services, data boundary, and support requirements.

capabilities.architectureNotes: Hybrid platforms extend management or provider infrastructure into customer-controlled locations. The options differ materially: managed hardware, connected management planes, and air-gapped deployments create different operating and compliance boundaries.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: Evaluate site readiness, network dependencies, patching ownership, disconnected operation, capacity planning, and data-boundary requirements before selecting an edge or on-premises extension.

aws.sourceNotes: Public documentation establishes AWS Outposts and AWS GovCloud offerings; confirm the required regulated deployment availability and service set with AWS before selection.

tierNotes.Personal / Free: Hardware-backed hybrid deployments are generally outside personal project needs.
tierNotes.Commercial / SMB: Assess site, connectivity, support, and minimum capacity requirements.
tierNotes.Enterprise: Plan hardware lifecycle, network resilience, local operations, and cloud service dependencies.
tierNotes.Government: Validate regulated-environment availability and service support for the intended facility.

azure.sourceNotes: Azure Arc documentation covers hybrid management; verify current Azure Government availability for the exact Arc-enabled resource types and extensions required.

tierNotes.Personal / Free: Use hybrid management only when off-cloud resources need common governance.
tierNotes.Commercial / SMB: Assess agent management, policy, monitoring, and connectivity requirements.
tierNotes.Enterprise: Standardize inventory, policy, security, observability, and change control across locations.
tierNotes.Government: Confirm the required Arc features and extensions against current Azure Government availability.

gcp.sourceNotes: Google documents connected and air-gapped Distributed Cloud variants; determine applicable regulatory authorization and supported services for the deployment.

tierNotes.Personal / Free: Dedicated hybrid hardware deployments are generally outside personal project needs.
tierNotes.Commercial / SMB: Assess site requirements, hardware model, connectivity, and supported services.
tierNotes.Enterprise: Plan fleet management, local operations, data placement, and disconnected-mode needs.
tierNotes.Government: Evaluate air-gapped requirements and the authorization scope for the intended workload.

capabilities.architectureNotes: Cost-governance services expose usage, budgets, allocation, optimization guidance, and reporting needed for accountable cloud operation. Their effectiveness depends on organizational scopes, tagging discipline, ownership, and timely review.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: Establish tagging and account hierarchy early, assign budget and anomaly-review ownership, and treat recommendations as inputs to engineering decisions rather than automatic actions.

aws.sourceNotes: AWS documents cost-management tooling and GovCloud separately; verify which billing, reporting, and optimization features are required and available for GovCloud accounts.

tierNotes.Personal / Free: Use cost visibility and budgets before adding material spend.
tierNotes.Commercial / SMB: Standardize account tags, budgets, cost allocation, and routine optimization review.
tierNotes.Enterprise: Establish FinOps ownership, multi-account reporting, commitment governance, and anomaly response.
tierNotes.Government: Confirm billing and reporting workflows for GovCloud organizations and procurement needs.

azure.sourceNotes: Microsoft documents Cost Management capabilities and Azure Government independently; verify billing scopes and feature availability in the target government environment.

tierNotes.Personal / Free: Set budgets and review cost analysis as resources are introduced.
tierNotes.Commercial / SMB: Use consistent tags, cost analysis, budgets, and optimization review.
tierNotes.Enterprise: Govern billing scopes, allocation, exports, commitments, and anomaly-response ownership.
tierNotes.Government: Validate cost-management capabilities and procurement reporting requirements in Azure Government.

gcp.govVariant: Cloud Billing API under Assured Workloads control packages
gcp.sourceNotes: Assured Workloads documentation identifies Cloud Billing API scope and limitations by control package; validate billing workflows for the selected package.

tierNotes.Personal / Free: Use billing visibility and budgets before introducing sustained spend.
tierNotes.Commercial / SMB: Adopt project labeling, budgets, reports, and regular optimization reviews.
tierNotes.Enterprise: Govern account exports, allocation, commitments, recommendations, and anomaly response.
tierNotes.Government: Confirm billing API and support-case scope for the selected Assured Workloads package.

capabilities.architectureNotes: Managed event services support decoupled integration through publish-subscribe, routing, and streaming patterns. Selection should be based on delivery semantics, ordering, retention, replay, throughput, and integration boundaries rather than service names alone.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: Document delivery guarantees and retry handling before implementation. Retention, dead-letter processing, replay, encryption, private connectivity, and audit access all affect operational and regulated workload design.

aws.sourceNotes: AWS publishes GovCloud service information separately; validate EventBridge features, integrations, and quotas required by a regulated workload before asserting availability or parity.

tierNotes.Personal / Free: Use simple event routing only where asynchronous integration improves the design.
tierNotes.Commercial / SMB: Establish event schemas, retries, dead-letter handling, and cost monitoring.
tierNotes.Enterprise: Govern event ownership, routing policies, replay needs, observability, and cross-account access.
tierNotes.Government: Confirm EventBridge support and required event targets in the selected AWS GovCloud architecture.

azure.sourceNotes: Microsoft maintains Azure Government service availability separately; verify Event Grid features and integrations on the current roadmap for the target environment.

tierNotes.Personal / Free: Use event routing for small integrations with explicit retry behavior.
tierNotes.Commercial / SMB: Standardize event subscriptions, delivery handling, private access, and monitoring.
tierNotes.Enterprise: Govern event domains, access policy, delivery assurance, and downstream dependencies.

capabilities.architectureNotes: Posture-management services aggregate configuration findings, exposure signals, and security recommendations. This is distinct from SIEM: posture management focuses on resource state and control drift, while SIEM focuses on event collection and investigation workflows.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: Enabling a posture service is not equivalent to meeting a compliance requirement. Assign remediation ownership, define exception handling, connect findings to ticketing or response processes, and validate the standards or control mappings applicable to the workload.
